name: Breaker
tagline: A three-step setup, a real Logs tab, and problem reports from inside the app.

highlights.title: Setup is three screens
highlights.body: Terms, sign in, local playback — that is the whole wizard now, in a plain WinUI dialog with an animated hero beside each step. The appearance, sidebar, sound and notification tour pages are gone; those choices live in Settings with the same defaults, and the dialog opens the moment Wavee does.

media.alt: The new setup dialog: the licence and terms page, with the sign-in page in front showing a QR code to scan

highlights.title: A real Logs tab
highlights.body: Settings › Logs is a full-height log viewer: a command bar to refresh, copy, export and open the log folder, a search box with level and category filters, rows that expand on a click to show their fields and exception, a session picker that lists your previous runs, and a Verbose switch that captures Debug and Trace for the running session.

media.alt: The Logs tab in Settings, listing log rows with level badges, a filter box and a command bar

highlights.title: Report a problem from inside Wavee
highlights.body: Settings › About has "Report a problem…" and "Suggest a feature…", and after a crash the next launch offers to file it. Wavee opens the matching GitHub form with the version, install source, architecture and Windows build filled in, and copies a redacted report — personal paths, account details, secrets and addresses removed — to your clipboard for you to paste.

media.alt: The Report a problem dialog with a title field, details box, a diagnostics checkbox and the redacted report preview
